acceptance_criteria: Integration tests: send MDN successfully → sent map has server-set fields + email gets $mdnsent; send to already-$mdnsent email → mdnAlreadySent; missing onSuccessUpdateEmail patch → invalidArguments rejection
description: Implement handle_mdn_send in src/mdn.rs. Sends RFC 5322 MDN messages and stamps $mdnsent via a coupled Email/set call.
design:
Request args: accountId, identityId, send: Id[MDN], onSuccessUpdateEmail: Id[PatchObject]|null.

Pre-flight checks (before calling backend):
1. Verify accountId exists; reject with invalidArguments if not.
2. Verify identityId exists and belongs to accountId; reject with invalidArguments if not.
3. For EACH entry in send map, verify onSuccessUpdateEmail contains a backward ref (#<creationId>) that sets keywords/$mdnsent: true. If ANY entry is missing this patch, reject the ENTIRE request with invalidArguments. Rationale: draft §2.1 — 'the server MUST reject an MDN/send which does not result in setting the keyword $mdnsent'.
4. Check $mdnsent keyword on the referenced email for each entry; if already set, add mdnAlreadySent SetError to notSent for that entry (do NOT send).

For each remaining entry (no pre-existing $mdnsent):
- Delegate to backend.send_mdns(account_id, identity_id, send_map).
- Backend returns server-set fields: finalRecipient, originalMessageId, mdnGateway, originalRecipient, error.
- On success: add to sent map with server-set fields only (omit fields client supplied).

After all sends succeed/fail:
- For each successfully sent entry, apply the corresponding onSuccessUpdateEmail patch via MailBackend::update_emails. This stamps $mdnsent on the source email.
- Response: { accountId, sent: Id[MDN]|null, notSent: Id[SetError]|null } + implicit Email/set response if any emails were updated.

SetError types: notFound (email not found or no Disposition-Notification-To header), forbidden, forbiddenFrom (finalRecipient not allowed by identity), overQuota, tooLarge, rateLimit, invalidProperties, mdnAlreadySent.

The 'using' property of the JMAP Request MUST include both urn:ietf:params:jmap:mdn and urn:ietf:params:jmap:mail — validate this in the handler.

Spec ref: draft-ietf-jmap-mdn-17 §2.1, §3.1.
notes:
CORRECTIONS (from research phase):

1. CRLF injection: After deserializing the Mdn struct, validate that subject, text_body, reporting_ua, and all extensionFields keys and values contain no CR or LF characters. Use check_no_crlf (made pub(crate) by JMAP-4ffm). On failure return SetError::invalid_properties for the specific creation-id entry.

2. forbiddenFrom: if the request Mdn for an entry has a non-null final_recipient, validate it matches a permitted address for the given identity. If not, return SetError of type ForbiddenFrom for that entry (not a whole-request rejection).

3. handle_mdn_send signature needs call_id: &str as third parameter (same pattern as handle_submission_set) so the implicit Email/set invocation can echo the same call_id.
   pub async fn handle_mdn_send<B: MailBackend + MdnBackend>(backend: &B, args: Value, call_id: &str) -> Result<(Value, Vec<Invocation>), JmapError>

4. The implicit Email/set: call backend.update_object::<Email>() for each successfully-sent entry's onSuccessUpdateEmail patch. Validate patch with find_immutable_patch_key before calling. Build Email/set response JSON and push to extra Vec<Invocation> with the same call_id. Do not dispatch through Dispatcher — this is identical to how submission.rs builds the companion Email/set response.
title: mdn: MDN/send handler
